title: k-producer — Kafka probe
description: Latency, delivery reconciliation and Kafka client health for the k-producer probe. Built from the metrics the application actually exports.

panels.title: Delivery integrity — did anything get lost?
Messages lost
panels.description: Sequences settled without ever arriving, over the dashboard time range. This is the loss figure. Anything above zero is real loss, not reordering.

panels.title: Duplicates
panels.description: Same sequence delivered more than once — at-least-once redelivery, or a consumer group rebalance replaying uncommitted offsets.

panels.title: Out of order
panels.description: Arrived below the high-water sequence. Expected with multiple partitions; unexpected on a single-partition topic.

panels.title: In flight
panels.description: Issued but neither received nor yet settled. Should hover near zero and return to zero after the publisher stops.

panels.title: Foreign (other runs)
panels.description: Messages from a previous run id, correctly excluded from reconciliation. High values mean backlog on the topic — see the latency caveat below.

panels.title: Produced vs received
panels.description: These two lines should sit on top of each other. A sustained gap is loss in progress; a transient gap is in-flight latency.

panels.title: Delivery anomalies
panels.description: 'late' means it arrived after being written off as missing — the window was too small, or recovery took longer than the window.

options.content:
**Role decides what this measures.** `loopback` = one-way, single process. `origin` = full round
trip via the echo instance. Both are timed on one clock, so no clock-skew correction is involved —
but never compare a `loopback` series against an `origin` series, they measure different journeys.

**Backlog inflates these panels.** Latency is recorded for every message with a parseable
timestamp, *including messages left on the topic by earlier runs* — unlike the reconciliation
counters above, which exclude them by run id. A consumer resuming from committed offsets, or
running with `autoOffsetReset=earliest`, replays days-old messages and drives the `+Inf` bucket and
the mean far beyond anything real. If `Foreign (other runs)` above is large, treat the percentiles
here as suspect and prefer the SLO attainment panel, which is bounded.

panels.title: Latency percentiles
panels.description: Interpolated from SLO buckets (1ms..30s). A p99 pinned at +Inf means samples exceeded the largest bucket — usually replayed backlog, occasionally real stalls.

panels.title: SLO attainment — share of messages under each threshold
panels.description: Bounded and backlog-resistant: a flood of ancient messages pushes these down rather than off the scale. The most trustworthy latency view.

panels.title: Latency by role and zone
panels.description: Split out so an origin in one zone and an echo in another stay distinguishable.

panels.title: Send rate — application vs Kafka client
panels.description: Divergence means records are being accepted by the client but not acknowledged by the broker — check the error and retry panel.

panels.title: Acknowledgement latency
panels.description: App-level ack latency includes client-side queueing; the client's request latency is broker round trip only. The gap between them is time spent batching.

panels.title: Errors and retries
panels.description: Retries rising while errors stay flat is the signature of a broker election or a transient partition leader change — recovery working.

panels.title: Buffer pressure
panels.description: Available falling toward zero means production is outpacing delivery; the next step is blocked sends and then max.block.ms timeouts.

panels.title: Producer queueing
panels.description: Queue time is how long a record waits before being sent. A rising wait ratio means the buffer pool is saturated.

panels.title: Consumer lag
panels.description: Records behind the partition head. Sustained growth means the consumer cannot keep up, or was paused. This is the single most important consumer-side signal.

panels.title: Age of consumed records
panels.description: How old a record was when consumed, from the broker's own timestamp. Unlike end-to-end latency this needs no shared clock with the producer.

panels.title: Offset progress by partition
panels.description: A flat line on one partition while others advance points at a stuck partition leader or an unbalanced assignment.

options.content:
This is the row for the tool's failure-testing purpose. When a broker is killed, the sequence to
watch is: **assigned partitions** drops → **rebalance rate** spikes → **connection creation**
climbs as clients reconnect → lag and in-flight messages drain back to baseline. The time from the
drop to lag returning to baseline is the recovery time.

**Caveat:** `assigned partitions` is reported by the client from its own cached group state. If
*every* broker becomes unreachable the client cannot learn it lost its partitions, so this can stay
flat at its last value through a total outage. Corroborate with connection and request rates, which
do fall to zero.

panels.title: Partition assignment
panels.description: Drops to zero during a rebalance and recovers. A prolonged zero means the consumer is not attached and nothing is being read.

panels.title: Rebalance activity
panels.description: Repeated rebalancing without recovery usually means a session timeout shorter than the poll interval, not a broker fault.

panels.title: Last rebalance
panels.description: Seconds since the consumer last rebalanced. Resets on every membership change, so a small number during a test means churn.

panels.title: Producer in-flight requests
panels.description: Pinned at max.in.flight with a flat send rate means the producer is blocked waiting on the broker.

panels.title: Heartbeat rate
panels.description: Falls to zero when the group coordinator is unreachable — often the earliest signal of broker trouble.

panels.title: Connection churn
panels.description: A burst of creates and closes is reconnection after a broker restart. Sustained churn is an unstable network path or a flapping broker.

panels.title: Broker request rates
panels.description: Requests continuing while responses fall to zero is the clearest picture of brokers that are addressable but not answering.

panels.title: Relay throughput
panels.description: Only present on instances running myapp.role=echo. Zero while an origin is publishing means the return leg is broken and round-trip latency will show nothing at all.

panels.title: JVM memory
panels.description: The probe should be flat and boring. Growth here means the tool itself is the problem, not the cluster.

list.name: instance_label
list.label: Instance label
list.description: The app tags every metric with `instance`, which collides with the target label Prometheus adds. A default scrape renames the app's copy to exported_instance; switch to `instance` if you scrape with honor_labels: true.

list.name: role
list.label: Role
list.description: loopback = one-way, origin = round trip, echo = relay.
